PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 06/15/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent edema, and reassessment of mental health treatment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately six weeks after his last visit. He reports that after the referral to the pulmonologist, he was started on a systemic corticosteroid regimen, which has provided some relief. He notes a decrease in nocturnal wheezing and a reduction in daytime dyspnea, allowing him to engage in light activities without significant discomfort. However, he still relies on the albuterol inhaler approximately six times daily, indicating that his COPD management plan requires further optimization.
Despite the improvement in respiratory symptoms, Mr. Fairfax continues to experience significant bilateral lower extremity edema, which remains at a 3+ pitting level. He reports that the nephrologist suggested an increase in the furosemide dosage to 120 mg daily, which he has been compliant with, but he has not noted substantial improvement. He expresses concern regarding the ongoing discomfort and the potential impact on his mobility.
Regarding his mental health, Mr. Fairfax states that he has been referred to a psychiatrist who adjusted his sertraline dosage to 100 mg daily. He reports some improvement in mood but continues to experience episodes of anxiety, particularly related to his physical health and limitations. He expresses a desire to explore additional therapeutic options, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) or mindfulness practices.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + improved dyspnea, + decreased nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + ongoing joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (increased dosage). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily (adjusted for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 84, BP 128/75, RR 24, O2 sat 82% on room air
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but more engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 10.5, Hct 31.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.2, Cl 101, CO2 29, BUN 30, Cr 1.8, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 600 (decreased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.0 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax shows improvement in respiratory symptoms with the corticosteroid regimen but continues to require frequent use of his albuterol inhaler. A referral for pulmonary rehabilitation is recommended to enhance his exercise capacity and overall lung function. Continued monitoring of his COPD symptoms and inhaler use is warranted. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite increased furosemide dosage. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended to assess renal function and potentially consider alternative diuretics or adjunct therapies. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax reports slight improvement with the adjusted sertraline dosage. A referral for CBT is advised to provide coping strategies for anxiety and to further address his depressive symptoms. Follow-up with psychiatry in one month for ongoing management.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
